races.name: Country And Western Raceday - 28th June Handicap

runners_data.name: White Umbrella

runners_data.comment: Her last four wins have been at this track and she was placed over C&D on penultimate run

runners_data.name: Punchbowl Flyer
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner likely to get uncontested lead, in good form and drawn better than last time
runners_data.comment: In-form 9yo but he's had only one win since June 2021
runners_data.spotlight: Series of creditable efforts this year and his front-running third over C&D last time was from a wide draw; should go well again off an unchanged mark but he's had only one win since June 2021.

runners_data.name: Twilight Madness
runners_data.note: Prominent runner coming off quick turnaround after Bath win, needs to avoid traffic in congested tactical position
runners_data.comment: Won at Bath on his penultimate run and is a big player if he can recapture that form
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-time sprint winner who scored at Bath (5f, good) two weeks ago and the quick turnaround may have caused his downfall at Kempton three days later; has claims if he can recapture that penultimate form and his four runs over C&D include a win and two thirds; dangerous.

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Front-running winner last time now carrying penalty, faces more pace pressure than at Pontefract
runners_data.comment: Made all at Pontefract and he's respected under a penalty on this step back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form when making all off a reduced mark at Pontefract (5f, good to soft) ten days ago; remains feasibly treated under a penalty and his four runs over this trip include a creditable third over C&D; respected.

runners_data.name: Style King
runners_data.note: Prominent type with Silvestre De Sousa up but poor recent form and needs to bounce back from disappointing efforts
runners_data.comment: Won at Lingfield in the autumn but he's been disappointing since and others are preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Made the breakthrough with a front-running win at Lingfield (6f, AW) in September but he's been disappointing since; may have needed his reappearance run last month but he's now 1-14 and this looks tough from a wide draw.

runners_data.name: Travel Agent
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in good form who should benefit from expected pace battle ahead of him
runners_data.comment: Close second at Kempton last week and he's a key player off same mark here

runners_data.name: Good Karma
runners_data.note: Patient type with claiming jockey who ran well here before but inconsistent and needs career-best effort
runners_data.comment: Disappointing when favourite at Thirsk latest and all of his three wins have been over 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Went close here (7f) on his penultimate run but he's not easy to predict and was well held when favourite at Thirsk (7f, good) last Friday; needs to step up again after that and all of his three wins have been over 7f; first-time visor.

runners_data.name: Due Date
runners_data.note: Prominent runner struggling for form this year despite being 2lb lower than last winning mark
runners_data.comment: On handy mark but he's been out of sorts this year and needs to get back on track
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins in a purple patch in the second half of 2025; now 2lb lower than for his last success but he's struggled at big prices in four runs this year and needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Megaphone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with long absence and poor recent form, needs significant improvement to feature

races.paceDynamic: Punchbowl Flyer will set the pace as the only confirmed front runner, likely getting an uncontested lead early. Behind him, Twilight Madness, Jojo Rabbit, Style King and Due Date will create a prominent traffic jam, with all four wanting the same tactical position tracking the leader. This congestion will force some to race wider or get shuffled back, creating gaps for the hold-up trio of White Umbrella, Travel Agent and Good Karma to exploit late. The uncontested leader scenario combined with prominent chaos strongly favours both the lone pace-setter and the patient hold-up horses who can avoid the mid-race scrimmaging.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Punchbowl Flyer gets a soft lead without early pressure from the prominent brigade.
scenarios.body: The 9-year-old can dictate terms and kick clear when the prominent pack starts battling each other. His recent third from a wide draw shows he's in good form and an easier passage here makes him very dangerous.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet create a messy pace battle that compromises each other 2-3 furlongs out.
scenarios.body: White Umbrella and Travel Agent can sweep up late as they avoid the traffic problems that will plague the prominent runners. Both have shown good recent form and this tactical setup plays to their strengths perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of Twilight Madness, Jojo Rabbit or Due Date gets first run on the leader while avoiding the worst of the traffic.
scenarios.body: The horse that positions best from the prominent pack can bridge the gap to Punchbowl Flyer and outstay him in the final furlong. Recent winner Twilight Madness looks the most likely to execute this.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Punchbowl Flyer goes too fast early trying to shake off persistent prominent pressure.
scenarios.body: The entire field comes back to the patient hold-up horses who get a perfect setup from off the pace. This requires the prominent horses to press harder than ideal, which seems unlikely given the lack of natural pace.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems 2-3 furlongs out when Twilight Madness, Jojo Rabbit, Style King and Due Date converge on the same prominent position
Monitor Punchbowl Flyer's early fractions - if he goes too fast trying to shake off pressure he becomes vulnerable late
Keep an eye on White Umbrella's position turning for home as she needs a clear run to utilise her strong finishing kick
Watch for Travel Agent getting squeezed up if the pace collapses suddenly as hold-up horses can get trapped
Observe how Jojo Rabbit handles the step back up to 6f under penalty pressure after his 5f Pontefract success

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Scheffler

runners_data.spotlight: 62,000euros yearling; 11-1 with blinkers applied on Lingfield debut (7f, Polytrack) last month but he didn't get much luck before finishing well for third; that was eye-catching and he's a big player if he can build on that on this drop in trip.

runners_data.name: Mayflower Rock
runners_data.note: Newcomer with unknown style, half-sister to decent winners but Dylan Cunha's moderate trainer record raises questions
runners_data.comment: Half-sister to two winners at up to 1m and market should guide on debut

runners_data.name: Sargent Dennis

runners_data.name: Kiani King
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced with unknown best style, 45 days off and disappointing C&D debut suggests limited ability

runners_data.spotlight: Faded into a well-held fourth of six on C&D debut last month and he recorded an RPR of 53 in that race; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Cool Doc Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 144-day break, runner-up on debut suggests ability but long absence raises fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Looks interesting on his debut second at Kempton and he's respected back from a break

runners_data.name: Goldenstateofmind
runners_data.note: Prominent style with 321 days off, gelded since disappointing Chester run and De Sousa booking significant
runners_data.comment: Disappointing in his second 2yo run and has something to prove after 11 months off
runners_data.spotlight: Made a promising start when runner-up at Thirsk (5f, good) last May but he was well held when upped to 6f at Chester four weeks later; gelded since and has something to prove after 11 months off.

runners_data.name: Hamda's Joy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with consistent place record on AW, 195-day absence major concern despite previous course form
runners_data.comment: Placed in two AW runs in the autumn but she was beaten 5l when odds-on last time
runners_data.spotlight: Finished third in two AW runs in the autumn but she was beaten 5l when odds-on at Newcastle (6f, Tapeta) last time; returns after 195 days off and she needs improvement to make a major impact here.

runners_data.name: Afton Down
runners_data.note: Natural leader with solid recent form, 169 days off but Fallon's booking and previous 6f form encouraging signs

races.paceDynamic: Hamda's Joy and Afton Down are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early pace, creating an honest gallop from the start. With two natural leaders and several prominent racers (Cool Doc Boy, Goldenstateofmind, Hallandale Beach), the pace will be solid throughout the 6f trip. The hold-up horses Scheffler and Sargent Dennis may struggle to get into contention if the pace becomes overly strong, while the prominent racers could find themselves in the firing line. This pace scenario strongly favours horses with early pace who can sit just off the leaders - the prominent runners will have the best tactical position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Cool Doc Boy or Goldenstateofmind can settle just behind the leading pair
scenarios.body: The two front-runners will soften each other up, allowing the prominent racers to strike in the final furlong with fresher legs. Cool Doc Boy showed promise on debut and returns from a break, while Goldenstateofmind has been gelded and brings solid form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If either Hamda's Joy or Afton Down can establish a clear lead without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The winner will dictate terms and have enough left to resist late challenges, particularly if the prominent horses get caught in traffic. Afton Down has the stronger recent form and Cieren Fallon's booking suggests confidence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes unsustainably fast between the two leaders
scenarios.body: Scheffler could benefit from a strong finish if the front-runners and prominent racers tire, though his style makes him vulnerable on this sharp track. The blinkers application suggests connections expect improvement from his Lingfield third.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Mayflower Rock shows significant improvement on debut or Kiani King finds notable progression
scenarios.body: The lightly-raced newcomer or an improver could exploit tactical pace scenarios, though both face questions about readiness and ability. Morrison's booking of Shepherd for Kiani King suggests some confidence despite poor trainer form.

watchPoints.text: Hamda's Joy and Afton Down could go too fast early and collapse, opening the door for prominent runners to sweep past
Cool Doc Boy's 144-day absence may tell in the final stages despite his early promise on debut
Scheffler needs the front-runners to overdo it but his hold-up style is poorly suited to this sharp 6f track
Mayflower Rock is a complete unknown quantity making her debut for a trainer with moderate recent form
The pace battle between the two leaders will determine whether prominent or hold-up horses can benefit most

races.name: Get The Inside Track With raceday-ready.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Crackergee
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 130-day break with tongue-tie removed, wildly inconsistent

runners_data.spotlight: Has ability but has also proved wildly inconsistent and is now 0-9; probably best watched with tongue-tie removed on return from 130 days off.

runners_data.name: Solar Pass

runners_data.comment: Winning return at Southwell last month; has run well over this far on turf; major player
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed filly who has proved consistent on the AW (721421), doubling her tally with a game success at Southwell (1m4f, Tapeta) last month after 182 days off (third and fourth won next time); only 3lb higher and has run well over this far on turf; major player.

races.paceDynamic: Robusto will take this race on from the front with his confirmed leading style, likely getting an easy time of things with Diamond Bay and Baileys Khelstar as the only other prominent runners but both coming off poor recent efforts. The pace will be manageable rather than fierce, with three hold-up horses (Caramay, Crackergee, Solar Pass) needing to rely on tactical speed from the back. With soft fractions likely and plenty of stamina required at 1m6f, this tactical setup strongly favours the front runner and any horse that can sit close to the pace early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Robusto gets an uncontested lead and maintains his rhythm
scenarios.body: The manageable pace allows him to dictate throughout while the hold-up horses face a difficult task from too far back. His stamina and tactical advantage from the front prove decisive despite recent poor form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Bay or Baileys Khelstar can sit close and kick when Robusto tires
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners overcomes recent disappointments to track the leader and strike in the final furlong. The pace scenario suits those who can be handy throughout the contest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and the front runners stop
scenarios.body: Caramay or Solar Pass benefit from their proven AW form and finishing kick to reel in tired leaders. The race becomes a sprint from the back with class telling late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Crackergee shows his best form fresh from the layoff
scenarios.body: The inconsistent sort finds his A-game returning from 130 days off and benefits from reduced weight. His hold-up style works if the pace is genuine enough to set up his finishing kick.

watchPoints.text: Robusto could get an uncontested lead and prove very hard to peg back despite recent poor form
Diamond Bay's last run was abysmal but he has winning course form at this distance
Baileys Khelstar was beaten 30+ lengths last time which raises serious questions about wellbeing
Crackergee returns fresh with equipment change after 130 days but has been inconsistent
Solar Pass drops back in trip from recent 1m4f win which could suit her finishing kick better

runners_data.spotlight: Made it 2-2 over C&D when scraping home last month; up 2lb, but that latest run came after 79 days off so he could be a bit sharper for it; high on list.

runners_data.name: Alondra
runners_data.note: Hold-up style mare with strong top-class jockey booking but faces tactical disadvantage over minimum trip despite solid C&D record
runners_data.comment: Record over C&D in February read 112, but seemed to be beaten fair and square last time
runners_data.spotlight: Record over C&D in February read 112, but she seemed to be beaten fair and square back here last month; the handicapper may have her for the time being.

races.paceDynamic: Gold Star Hero will likely lead from the outset, having made virtually all to win over 6f here eight days ago, with Counsel, Accrual, and Ziggy's Missile content to track in prominent positions. The sole confirmed front-runner faces no obvious pace pressure, allowing him to dictate fractions and potentially string out the field over this minimum trip. With most rivals possessing prominent or hold-up styles, Gold Star Hero can control the tempo and kick clear in the final furlong. This pace dynamic strongly favours the leader and prominent racers who can stay close to the pace, as hold-up horses will struggle to make up ground over 5f from midfield or worse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gold Star Hero Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Gold Star Hero breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure from prominent runners
scenarios.body: He can dictate ideal fractions and kick clear turning for home, with the field strung out behind him over the minimum trip. His recent 6f course win suggests he has the pace to lead and the stamina to last home over 5f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace Duel
scenarios.trigger: If Counsel or Accrual press Gold Star Hero early, creating genuine pace pressure
scenarios.body: The increased tempo will set up the race for a closer who can finish strongly, with the early leaders potentially weakening in the final furlong. Alondra's hold-up style becomes an asset if she can get a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ziggy's Missile Returns
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Missile shows his old C&D form despite the 175-day absence
scenarios.body: His previous 1st and 2nd place finishes over C&D when returning from breaks suggest he handles fresh returns well. The prominent style allows him to track Gold Star Hero and challenge late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Havana Blast Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses and becomes tactical, suiting hold-up horses
scenarios.body: Havana Blast can use his late kick to maximum effect, though he'll need the leaders to come back to him significantly. His sole win came with first-time tongue-tie at Chelmsford over this trip.

watchPoints.text: Gold Star Hero breaks slowly or gets pressured early, as his front-running style is crucial to his chances and any disruption changes the race dynamic completely
Ziggy's Missile shows early pace despite the 175-day layoff, as his historical C&D returns suggest he could outrun his odds if fully fit
Counsel travels keenly in the early stages, as he needs to stay prominent but not waste energy fighting for position behind Gold Star Hero
The pace becomes crawling in the first two furlongs, as this would bring hold-up horses like Havana Blast and Alondra right into contention
Alondra gets a clear run in the final furlong, as her hold-up style requires racing room to be effective over this sharp 5f trip

runners_data.spotlight: Comfortably held in two starts at Southwell (1m/7f) last month; handicaps become an option after this.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Writer stands out as the sole confirmed front runner with proven form on this surface, likely to dictate terms from the front without serious early pressure. The prominent runners (Grow Old With Me, Law Court, Slight Of Foot, Korbut) will settle just behind, while hold-up horses (Luansobe, Ahead Of Fashion, Battle Standard) track from the rear. With limited early pace pressure, Mr Writer can control fractions and kick clear, making this a race that clearly favours front runners and prominent racers who can track the pace without getting too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Writer gets an uncontested lead and controls the pace
scenarios.body: Mr Writer's proven AW form and tactical advantage from the front allows him to dictate ideal fractions before kicking clear. The lack of serious pace pressure means he can save energy for a decisive move entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners can track Mr Writer closely and outkick him
scenarios.body: Grow Old With Me or Law Court use their class to sit just off the pace before delivering a sustained challenge. Their superior ratings and fresher profiles give them the edge in a finish where early positioning proves crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debut Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If either Beautiful Rumour or Anton Mauve shows significant market support indicating readiness
scenarios.body: One of the well-bred newcomers produces a debut performance that catches the exposed runners off guard. Their connections' recent form and pedigrees suggest they could be ready to win first time out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Challenge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly dawdling and suits the closers
scenarios.body: Luansobe or another hold-up horse benefits from a slow pace that allows them to close strongly. However, Mr Writer's likely tactical control makes this scenario unlikely on a sharp 7f trip.

races.paceDynamic: Tryst and Politely are both confirmed front runners who will clash from the start, creating an honest early gallop over this extended mile trip. With Just A Girl also showing prominent tendencies, the early pace should be solid rather than crawling, particularly given the small field size means less tactical maneuvering. The two hold-up horses, Orangesandlemons and Maeva, will need the pace to collapse or maintain strong finishing kicks. This race shape clearly favors the prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Duel Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Tryst and Politely engage in a sustained speed battle through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The two leaders weaken each other, allowing the prominent Just A Girl to inherit the lead turning for home while the closers pick up the pieces late. This favors horses with tactical pace who avoided the early war.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dominant Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders (likely Tryst given superior rating) establishes a clear advantage early
scenarios.body: The winner controls fractions and kicks clear, with the pace strong enough to prevent a closer's challenge but not suicidal. Tryst's Wolverhampton course experience becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Special
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes modest with the leaders respecting each other
scenarios.body: Maeva and Orangesandlemons get the perfect setup for their finishing kicks, with the race becoming a sprint from the two-furlong pole. Maeva's class advantage shows.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Just A Girl uses her prominent style to grab an early position behind the leaders
scenarios.body: She avoids the pace battle while staying close enough to strike, benefiting from both the setup and her recent course experience at similar all-weather tracks.

races.paceDynamic: Naughty Niall will set the pace from his prominent position, but won't be pressured by any genuine speed merchants in this field. The lack of early pace means the tempo will be manageable through the middle sections, allowing the large cohort of hold-up horses to get into contention. With most runners preferring to come from behind, this sets up a sprint finish where positioning and timing will be crucial. This sustainable pace strongly favours hold-up horses who can unleash late kicks, particularly those with proven finishing speed at this venue.

scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows closers to get perfect positioning, setting up a cavalry charge in the final two furlongs where pure finishing speed decides it
